propositions: Gold-pair decision-flip computation at parity.py:107 counts a pair as a flip when a synthetic `decision="dropped"` on an errored side differs from the other side's real verdict, without guarding on the `errored` flag.
Errored records are admitted to gold_pairs via gold label membership alone (parity.py:105), not decision vocabulary membership, so no decision value can exempt them.

A single transient error on one arm causes the parity slot to fail criterion (b) by reporting one fabricated flip, despite criterion (d) already gating error rate separately, resulting in double-counting.

Three arms with (A) 3 real flips + 0 errors, (B) 2 real flips + 1 error, and (C) 0 real flips + 3 errors all report identical `decision_flips=3` with no per-pair detail to distinguish fabricated from genuine flips.
The silent case of `errored=True, valid=True` records produce `decision_flips=1` with no corroborating signal in validity or error-rate metrics.

The fix excludes pairs where either side has `errored=True` from decision_flips, counts them separately into `errored_pairs` metric, and surfaces the exclusion in gating failure strings without changing recorded live-run metrics.
